issues.legal_issue: A building patta does not transfer the site to the building owner unless that person already owned the site before the appointed day.
material_facts: The land was formerly minor inam land, and a tenant had constructed a building on it.
The settlement authority granted a ground-rent patta for the building to the tenant who owned it and a patta for the site to the former inamdar.
The tenant claimed that the building patta also made him owner of the site.
issues.conclusion: The building patta did not vest the site in the tenant; the site vested in the person who owned it immediately before the appointed day.
issues.legal_principle: Section 13(1) of the Madras Minor Inams (Abolition and Conversion into Ryotwari) Act, 1963 provides that a building vests in the person who owned it immediately before the appointed day. Section 13(2), which includes the building site within the meaning of building, does not transfer the site to a building owner who did not previously own it. The Court agreed with Sri Kumarakattalai Subrahmanyaswami Devasthanam v. K.S. Sunderarajulu Chettiar, ILR (1975) 1 Mad 501.

predicates.minor_inam_settlement_case: The dispute concerns land undergoing conversion from minor inam tenure through a settlement process.
predicates.building_owned_by_one_person: A person other than the site owner owned the building on the land immediately before the relevant appointed day.
predicates.site_previously_owned_by_another: A different person owned the site immediately before the relevant appointed day.

issues.definition: When a minor-inam settlement concerns a building owned by one person on a site previously owned by another, the site remains with the person previously entitled to it.

issues.legal_issue: A ryotwari patta granted in a revenue settlement does not, by itself, adjudicate civil title to the land.
material_facts: The settlement authority granted pattas following the abolition of minor inams.
The patta identified the tenant as entitled in respect of the building and the former inamdar as entitled in respect of the site.
The tenant relied on the patta to claim ownership of the site and to defeat the former inamdar's claim.
issues.conclusion: The grant of a ryotwari patta was a revenue settlement and did not determine title to the land.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 3, 8, 11 and 12 of the Madras Minor Inams (Abolition and Conversion into Ryotwari) Act, 1963 establish a process for vesting minor inams in the Government, determining entitlement to ryotwari pattas, and collecting land revenue. Sections 43 and 46 make decisions binding or final only as to matters falling within the statutory process. The Court relied on State of Tamil Nadu v. Ramalinga Samigal Madam, AIR 1986 SC 794, concerning the limited revenue purpose of settlement decisions, and distinguished Vatticherukuru Village Panchayat v. Nori Venkatarama Deekshithulu, [1991] 2 SCR 531, which concerned a matter entrusted to revenue authorities for determination.

predicates.minor_inam_revenue_settlement_case: The proceeding concerns a revenue settlement arising from the conversion of minor inam land.
predicates.settlement_authority_granted_ryotwari_pa: A settlement authority issued a ryotwari patta in the course of that revenue settlement.

issues.definition: A patta issued in a minor-inam revenue settlement does not adjudicate civil title when the proceeding is a revenue settlement and the settlement authority has issued the patta.

issues.legal_issue: A civil court retains jurisdiction over a claim to recover land or evict a tenant, and a patta does not nullify a civil decree on that claim.
material_facts: A landholder brought a civil suit seeking recovery of land from a tenant on grounds including non-payment of rent, and obtained a decree.
Before the decree, a settlement authority had issued a joint patta identifying the tenant in relation to the building and the landholder in relation to the site.
The execution court treated the patta as changing the tenant's status and preventing execution of the decree.
The civil claim concerned recovery and eviction, matters not determined by the patta grant.
issues.conclusion: The civil court's jurisdiction was not ousted, and the patta did not make the decree a nullity or prevent its execution; the matter was remitted for fresh disposal.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 43(1) and 43(2) of the Madras Minor Inams (Abolition and Conversion into Ryotwari) Act, 1963 make decisions binding only on matters within the respective statutory and civil-court jurisdictions. Section 46 gives finality to decisions only on matters to be determined for the purposes of the Act. The Court relied on State of Tamil Nadu v. Ramalinga Samigal Madam, AIR 1986 SC 794, and distinguished Vatticherukuru Village Panchayat v. Nori Venkatarama Deekshithulu, [1991] 2 SCR 531, because the dispute here concerned a landlord's claim to recover land from a tenant rather than a matter entrusted to the settlement authorities.

predicates.civil_recovery_or_eviction_proceeding: A civil proceeding seeks recovery of land or eviction of a tenant.
predicates.civil_decree_on_recovery_or_eviction: A civil court has issued a decree deciding the recovery or eviction claim.
predicates.revenue_patta_does_not_determine_that_cl: A revenue authority has issued a patta, but its decision does not address the civil recovery or eviction claim.

issues.definition: When a civil court has decided a recovery or eviction claim and a revenue patta does not decide that claim, the civil court retains jurisdiction and the decree is not nullified.
